executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent biological threats across Europe and the Americas. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with pandemic spillover potential, a resurgent dengue season, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with continued respiratory virus co-circulation. Additional signals include mpox transmission in the Americas, rising pertussis cases, yellow fever activity, and measles importation risk in under-vaccinated populations.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous biological threats across the Americas and Europe demand heightened surveillance, with H5N1 and dengue representing the highest near-term escalation risks.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating continued and expanding H5N1 detections
Animal-to-human spillover risk with pandemic potential; alerts spanning multiple months suggest sustained enzootic activity
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at animal-human interface; enforce biosafety protocols at poultry and livestock farms; prepare antiviral stockpiles and monitor for human cases

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating above-baseline transmission across multiple countries
Historically high seasonal pressure in the Americas with multi-serotype co-circulation increasing severe disease risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, strengthen hospital surge capacity for severe dengue management, and issue public advisories in affected countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Respiratory Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Earlier January 2026 alert flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation, increasing healthcare burden and diagnostic complexity
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake in Southern Hemisphere countries; ensure adequate antiviral supplies; prepare ICU capacity for dual-pathogen respiratory season

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 documenting ongoing mpox transmission in the Americas
Persistent community transmission signals inadequate containment; risk of clade spread across borders
threats.action: Accelerate JYNNEOS vaccination in high-risk populations; strengthen case detection and contact tracing; coordinate cross-border surveillance

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO updates (December 2025 and March 2026) indicate sustained and potentially increasing pertussis activity
Resurgence pattern suggests waning vaccine immunity or surveillance gaps in infant and adolescent cohorts
threats.action: Review and bolster Tdap/DTaP vaccination coverage, particularly in infants and pregnant women; investigate clusters in countries with declining immunization rates

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active yellow fever transmission risk
Alert timing suggests epizootic or human case activity in endemic zones with risk of urban spread
threats.action: Ensure vaccination campaigns in at-risk populations; enforce vaccination requirements for travelers; strengthen sylvatic surveillance in jungle-border regions

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 citing measles activity and importation risk in the Americas
Suboptimal vaccination coverage in several countries creates susceptible cohorts vulnerable to outbreak amplification
threats.action: Audit MMR vaccination coverage at subnational level; implement rapid response immunization in under-vaccinated communities; strengthen airport and border-point surveillance

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling chikungunya activity
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika in Aedes-endemic areas complicates clinical differentiation and vector control prioritization
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance into existing arboviral monitoring systems; enhance vector control and community education in affected areas

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific alerts identified in the 21 reports; however, sustained Bordetella pertussis resurgence despite vaccination may warrant investigation into macrolide treatment response and potential reduced susceptibility

Broad antimicrobial use during co-circulating respiratory virus seasons (influenza, RSV, mpox) elevates risk of secondary bacterial infections treated empirically, potentially accelerating AMR selection pressure in the Americas
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory season onset in the Southern Hemisphere (influenza + RSV) mirrors patterns that previously overwhelmed healthcare systems in 2022-2023, suggesting compounding surge risk

Persistent and recurring H5N1 alerts across consecutive months (November 2025, March 2026) indicate endemic entrenchment in Americas animal reservoirs rather than episodic incursion, raising pandemic preparedness urgency

Arboviral co-circulation (Dengue, Chikungunya) alongside yellow fever activity in the Americas suggests broad Aedes aegypti vector amplification, potentially linked to climate-driven habitat expansion
Two consecutive pertussis updates spanning December 2025 to March 2026 indicate a multi-month resurgence wave, consistent with 4-5 year cyclical pertussis patterns seen globally post-COVID
Mpox persistence in the Americas despite available vaccines signals ongoing transmission in networks not yet reached by vaccination programs, with risk of clade diversification
